prompt: A clean botanical illustration of a sawn LOG END on a naturalist's study card, a round cross-section of a young trunk shown flat and straight-on, fine ink-and-wash rendering on off-white paper. The trunk must show EXACTLY 40 concentric annual GROWTH RINGS as thin brown lines around one central pith, counted as-is from the centre outward (do NOT default to an even decorative ring pattern or an arbitrary number -- there must be exactly 40 complete rings). Every other ring keeps the normal wide spacing. Delicate continuous ring lines, subtle wood tone. No text, no numbers, no labels, no scale bar.

Does the picture show a round wood cross-section with concentric ring lines? A realistic photo or an illustration BOTH count as yes.
